title: Fundamental groups of a dense open surject
statement:
Let $V$ be a connected normal Noetherian scheme, let
$k:V'\hookrightarrow V$ be a dense open immersion, and let $\bar v$ be a
geometric point of $V'$, with the fundamental groups of
[def-galois-fibre-functor].

1. (*Geometric surjectivity.*) The map
   $\pi_1(V',\bar v)\to\pi_1(V,\bar v)$ induced by pullback of finite
   etale covers is surjective. Equivalently, a connected finite etale
   cover of $V$ stays connected over $V'$.
2. (*Weil groups.*) Let $V_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme
   whose base change $V=V_0\times_{k_0}k$ is connected and normal, let
   $V'_0\subseteq V_0$ be a dense open, and put
   $V'=V'_0\times_{k_0}k$. Then the induced map of Weil groups
   $W(V'_0)\to W(V_0)$ of [def-wf-weil-group] commutes with the degree
   maps, restricts on the geometric subgroups to the surjection of (1),
   and is surjective.
3. (*Lisse sheaves extend uniquely.*) For every lisse sheaf
   $\mathcal N$ on $V$ (at every finite coefficient level in the convention of
   [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], and for lisse $\Qlb$-sheaves
   formed from compatible finite-level $\mathcal O_E$-models by
   inverting $\ell$ and extending coefficients to $\Qlb$, where
   $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite) the adjunction unit
   $\mathcal N\to k_*k^*\mathcal N$ is an isomorphism.
4. (*Restriction on curves.*) Let $U_0$ be a curve in the sense of
   [d-real-setup] and $k:U'_0\hookrightarrow U_0$ a nonempty open.
   Pullback $k^*$ from lisse Weil sheaves on $U_0$ to lisse Weil sheaves
   on $U'_0$ is fully faithful, and it carries irreducible objects (no
   lisse subsheaf other than $0$ and itself) to irreducible objects. The
   same holds for lisse $\Qlb$-sheaves on the geometric curves
   $U'\hookrightarrow U$.
5. (*Constructibility.*) If $j:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ is a nonempty
   open in a curve $C_0$ of [d-real-setup] and $\mathcal F$ is lisse on
   $U_0$, then the middle extension $j_*\mathcal F$ of
   [def-wf-middle-extension] is constructible at every finite
   coefficient level.

proof.text: Curve preliminaries for (4) and (5). From d-real-setup extract smoothness, finite type, quasi-compactness, dimension one and connectedness after algebraic closure. Use lem-weil-geometrically-connected-algebraic-closure to obtain geometric connectedness and hence connectedness over the finite field. The source Regular module supplies IsRegular.of_smooth and integrality/irreducibility of a connected regular locally Noetherian scheme. Its dimension formula converts the component dimension condition to SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1. These are the private curve_regular_connected and curve_relativeDimension helpers.

Clause (1a) reuses the already proved source declaration Scheme.FiniteEtale.isConnected_pullback_of_isIntegrallyClosed_stalk in WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.FundamentalGroup.DenseOpenNormal. A geometric point makes the open nonempty. The connected finite etale cover remains connected on any such open of a connected normal locally Noetherian scheme; the density hypothesis is redundant here. No decomposition theorem from Sheaf is needed.

Clause (1b) works directly on Aut of the finite-etale fibre functors. The normal stalks make V irreducible, and its nonempty open U is connected. Transport the natural action of Aut(fiber s) along pullbackFiberIso to fiber(s composed with j). Naturality is inherited from fibre automorphisms; continuity follows from the discrete finite fibres. For each connected cover, clause (1a) and the fibre-functor action give transitivity after this transport. Mathlib CategoryTheory.PreGaloisCategory.toAut_surjective_of_isPretransitive now gives surjectivity of the canonical fiberAutBaseChange. This avoids the open-subgroup separation and the FLC equivalence detour.

Clause (2). First descend normal stalks along the flat surjective algebraic-closure projection. For a faithfully flat map A to C of domains with C integrally closed, embed their fraction fields. An integral fraction a/b becomes an element s of C; then a=bs in C. Faithfully flat contraction of the principal ideal (b) implies a=br in A, so the fraction is r. Apply this to the local faithfully flat stalk maps. Connectedness descends through the surjective projection; finite type and quasi-compactness give Noetherianity. Clause (1b) therefore surjects on the arithmetic fibre automorphisms. Using the constantCoverFiberMap bijections and their Frobenius-power compatibility from the proved source RestrictionWeilGroup module, naturality identifies the two Weil-pair membership conditions. Map (g,n) to (r(g),n) and lift g through the arithmetic surjection. The degree is unchanged, so the same lift also proves surjectivity on degree-zero kernels. This is the private weilGroup_lift_surjective argument; no Weil exact sequence is used.

Clause (3) reuses the proved source normal-scheme unit results: Etale.isIso_unit_upperStarLowerStarAdjunction_of_isIntegrallyClosed_stalk in WeilConjectures.ConstructibleSheaf.DenseOpenUnitNormal at finite level, and ProEtale.IsAdicLisseSheaf.isIso_adicUpperStarLowerStarAdjunction_unit_app_of_isIntegrallyClosed in WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.ProEtale.Adic.DenseOpenUnit for algebraic adic coefficients. They apply to the given hV, j and density without replacing the category or the adjunction.

Clause (4) uses the curve preliminaries. The nonempty open is dense in the irreducible curve. Apply the already proved source WeilSheaf.IsLisse.upperStar, WeilSheaf.upperStar_map_bijective_of_isLisse and WeilSheaf.IsIrreducibleLisse.upperStar_of_isDominant in WeilConjectures.WeilSheaf.DenseOpen. For the geometric version, the displayed pullback.map is an open immersion by its cartesian square. Its domain is nonempty by surjectivity of algebraic-closure base change. Its target is connected, smooth, regular, locally Noetherian and quasi-compact, hence integral; thus the geometric open is dense. Apply the source ProEtale lisse pullback, Hom bijection and irreducible pullback results from LisseMonodromyPullback. No etale/adic representation equivalence is imported.

Clause (5). The curve preliminaries give that C is connected and regular, hence integral. The nonempty open U is regular and connected, hence integral and normal. Finite type and quasi-compactness are supplied by d-real-setup. Apply lem-fin-normal-open-lisse-image to the finite locally constant sheaf F: its ordinary lowerStar is exactly the finite-level middle extension in this clause.

proof_origin.place: Clauses (1)-(5), reusing the existing source normal dense-open and restriction APIs; faithfully flat normality descent and Weil-pair lifting proved explicitly; 2026-10-19

tool_uses.why: Step (1) needs the converse direction that every open subgroup is the stabilizer of a connected finite étale cover; the unit route provides only the Galois equivalence and the transitive-implies-connected fact is not stated there.
Step 0 needs the generic decomposition of a Noetherian normal scheme into normal integral open-and-closed components; this existing statement records the needed Stacks fact.
Generic smooth-curve normality supplies the normality hypotheses in (4) and (5); the unit uses this fact in Step 0 but does not prove it.

Step (2) must check that V_0 and V'_0 are geometrically connected, as the Weil-group definition and exact sequence require, from connectedness of their base changes to the algebraically closed k; the unit route does not state this. Added by the maintainer reader.

lean.note: All five clauses, in eight named statements. Uses the existing fiberAutBaseChange on full fibre-functor automorphism groups, avoiding extra connectedness/model hypotheses. The Weil-group types unfold the existing weilGroup/weilGroupDeg abbreviations to their recorded constant-cover fibre products, so geometric connectedness of the dense open is derived in the proof rather than assumed. The map is specified by its exact pair formula. Finite and algebraic-adic units, lisse Hom bijections and irreducibility, and finite-level constructibility are all retained.
